+# ===========================================================================
+# 01 — Basics: expressions, bindings, operators, if, blocks
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: everything in Rian is an EXPRESSION that yields a value — `if`,
+# `match`, and blocks included. There are no statements that don't produce a
+# value. This maps cleanly onto both targets (Rust if/match are expressions;
+# Elixir evaluates everything to a value).
+#
+# Spec: docs/spec/expressions.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Single-clause function. The typed head IS the type boundary — no separate
+# signature line is needed when there is exactly one clause.
+fn add(x i64, y i64) i64 := x + y
+
+# Block body: a `;`/newline-separated sequence of bindings whose value is the
+# LAST expression (implicit return). Bodies open after the return type and
+# close with `end`.
+fn double_then_inc(n i64) i64
+  d := n * 2          # `:=` is a single-assignment binding, never mutation
+  d + 1               # the final expression is the function's value
+end
+
+# `:=` is single-assignment and irrefutable. Re-using a name SHADOWS the old
+# binding (a fresh value), it does not mutate it. Mutation is a different
+# operator, `<-`, and is capability-gated (see 04_capabilities.rian).
+fn shadow_demo(n i64) i64
+  x := n + 1
+  x := x * 10         # shadow: a NEW `x`, the old one is untouched
+  x
+end
+
+# A value-position `if` REQUIRES `else` (both arms must have the same type),
+# exactly like Rust. An `else`-less `if` would be a unit-typed effect.
+fn sign(n i64) i64 := if n >= 0 do 1 else -1 end
+
+# else-if chains read top to bottom.
+fn grade(s i64) str :=
+  if s >= 90 do "A"
+  else if s >= 80 do "B"
+  else "C" end
+
+# Operator character (precedence tightest -> loosest, see the spec table):
+#   *  /  rem  div        `/` is FLOAT division; `div` is INTEGER division.
+#   +  -                  No "is `/` int or float?" ambiguity — ever.
+#   <>                    string / binary concatenation (right-assoc)
+#   |>                    pipe: threads the value as the FIRST argument
+#   <  <=  >  >=          NON-ASSOCIATIVE: `a < b < c` is a SYNTAX ERROR
+#   ==  !=                also non-associative
+#   and  or  not          short-circuit boolean operators
+fn mean(total f64, count f64) f64 := total / count    # float div
+fn idiv(a i64, b i64) i64         := a div b           # integer div
+fn parity(n i64) i64              := n rem 2
+
+# Concatenation and the pipe. `x |> f(y)` is exactly `f(x, y)`.
+# There is NO method-call syntax (`x.f(y)`); `.` accesses fields only.
+fn greet(name str) str := "hello, " <> name
+fn loud_greeting(name str) str := name |> greet |> String.upcase
+
+# Precedence is resolved by a precedence-climbing (Pratt) parser, so the
+# emitter parenthesizes correctly on both targets:
+#   a + b |> f   parses as  (a + b) |> f
+#   not a and b  parses as  (not a) and b
+fn worked(a i64, b i64, c i64) i64 := a + b * c        # == a + (b * c)

+# ===========================================================================
+# 02 — Type declarations & the `match` expression
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: three declaration keywords, each with a distinct, idiomatic
+# representation on BOTH targets — and `match` is an expression that the
+# exhaustiveness gate refuses to emit unless it is total.
+#
+#   type   -> sealed sum (ADT)  -> BEAM atom/tagged-tuple   | Rust `enum`
+#   struct -> product / record  -> BEAM `%Name{}` struct    | Rust `struct`
+#   alias  -> transparent synonym -> BEAM `@type` (transparent) | Rust `type X = ..`
+#
+# Spec: docs/spec/types-match.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Sum type with payload variants. Fields are written `label type` (a lowercase
+# name then the type, NO colon). Labels are compile-time ergonomics only and
+# are erased on the BEAM.
+type Shape := Circle(radius f64) | Square(side f64)
+
+# Simple enum (all nullary). Nullary variants lower to snake_case atoms on the
+# BEAM (`Red` -> `:red`) and to unit enum variants on Rust.
+type Color := Red | Green | Blue
+
+# Product / record type. Becomes `%Point{}` on the BEAM and a Rust `struct`.
+struct Point(x f64, y f64)
+
+# Transparent synonym. `Id` and `i64` are interchangeable; no runtime cost.
+alias Id := i64
+
+# --- `match` is an EXPRESSION (it yields a value) -------------------------
+# Arms use `->`; `fn` bodies use `:=`. Arm bodies are implicit blocks ending
+# at the next arm header or `end`. Exhaustiveness is STATIC and REQUIRED.
+
+fn area(Shape) f64
+fn area(s) :=
+  match s do
+    Circle(r) -> 3.14159265 * r * r
+    Square(s) -> s * s
+  end
+
+# A fuller worked example: a JSON shape. Note the recursive `JArr(Vec(Json))`
+# — recursion through `Vec` needs no extra Rust `Box` (Vec is already heap).
+# A guarded arm (`when ..`) does NOT count toward exhaustiveness, so the
+# unguarded `JNum(_)` arm backs the `JNum(n) when n == 0.0` arm.
+type Json :=
+    JNull
+  | JBool(bool)
+  | JNum(f64)
+  | JStr(str)
+  | JArr(Vec(Json))
+
+fn type_of(Json) str
+fn type_of(j) :=
+  match j do
+    JNull                 -> "null"
+    JBool(_)              -> "bool"
+    JNum(n) when n == 0.0 -> "zero"
+    JNum(_)               -> "number"
+    JStr(_)               -> "string"
+    JArr(_)               -> "array"
+  end
+
+# Construction uses positional or named args (named uses the `key: value`
+# association syntax shared with map literals):
+fn unit_circle() Shape := Circle(radius: 1.0)
+fn origin() Point      := Point(x: 0.0, y: 0.0)

+# ===========================================================================
+# 03 — Multi-clause functions, guards, exhaustiveness, partiality
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: a function is either a single typed clause, or a bodiless
+# SIGNATURE line followed by contiguous pattern-head clauses. Exhaustiveness
+# is checked statically and is STRICTER than Elixir — a non-total function is
+# a compile error, exactly as Rust requires.
+#
+# Spec: docs/spec/clauses-guards.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Multi-clause group: bodiless signature, then pattern clauses sharing the
+# name/arity. First match wins, top to bottom (Elixir `def` order / Rust
+# `match` arm order — identical on both targets).
+fn classify(i64) str
+fn classify(0)            := "zero"
+fn classify(n) when n > 0 := "positive"
+fn classify(_)            := "negative"
+
+# Guards are a RESTRICTED, pure, total sublanguage — the intersection of
+# Elixir guards and Rust match guards. Arbitrary calls are rejected; only a
+# fixed whitelist (comparisons, arithmetic, `in`, and `is_*`/`len`/`abs`)
+# is allowed, so guards stay portable to both targets.
+fn cmp(i64, i64) Order
+fn cmp(a, b) when a <  b := Less
+fn cmp(a, b) when a == b := Equal
+fn cmp(_, _)             := Greater
+
+# Union narrowing: a guard that narrows a union lowers to a GUARD on Elixir
+# but a PATTERN ARM on Rust (Rust narrows enums structurally). Same source,
+# two idiomatic shapes.
+fn show(i64 | str) str
+fn show(x) when is_int(x) := "int: " <> to_str(x)
+fn show(x) when is_str(x) := "str: " <> x
+
+# Exhaustiveness is enforced: GUARDED clauses do not count, so a guard-only
+# function needs an unguarded fallback. `max2`'s second clause is the
+# unguarded backstop that makes it total on both targets.
+fn max2(i64, i64) i64
+fn max2(a, b) when a >= b := a
+fn max2(a, b)             := b
+
+# Partiality is opt-in and never silent. Without `@partial`, omitting the
+# `None` case below is a COMPILE ERROR. With it, Rust emits a `panic!` arm and
+# Elixir relies on `FunctionClauseError`.
+@partial
+fn unwrap(Option(T)) T
+fn unwrap(Some(x)) := x
+
+# Reachability is checked too: a clause fully shadowed by earlier clauses is a
+# warning; two clauses with identical heads + guards is an error.

+# ===========================================================================
+# 04 — Reference capabilities: the heart of Rian
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: THIS is what makes Rian Rian. A parameter's *reference capability*
+# — `val` / `iso` / `ref` / `tag` — drives its Rust signature (owned vs
+# borrowed vs `&mut`) AND its BEAM-side linearity (use-once) guarantee. The
+# programmer NEVER writes a Rust lifetime; the capability produces the right
+# ownership automatically. The same source-level discipline catches the
+# "use a handle after it's consumed" bug on BOTH targets.
+#
+# Capabilities are written between the (optional) param name and its type:
+#       fn f(name CAP Type) Ret
+# The default capability is `val` (read-only borrow — the common, safe case).
+#
+# Spec: docs/spec/capability-lowering.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Rust parameter-type matrix this drives (every cell compiled by rustc):
+#
+#   capability | Copy prim |  str   | Vec(T)        | nominal (Shape)
+#   -----------|-----------|--------|---------------|----------------
+#   val        | i64 byval | &str   | &[f64]        | &Shape
+#   iso        | i64 move  | String | Vec<f64>      | Shape
+#   ref        | &mut i64  | &mut.. | &mut Vec<f64> | &mut Shape
+#   tag        | &i64      | &Str.. | &Vec<f64>     | &Shape
+
+# `val` (default): a read-only borrow. On Rust this is `&Shape` and uses the
+# idiomatic borrowed forms (`&str` not `&String`, `&[T]` not `&Vec<T>`). On the
+# BEAM a `val` is freely shareable — usable any number of times. That is WHY
+# `r * r` below is legal: `r` flows from a `val` parameter.
+fn area(s val Shape) f64
+fn area(Circle(r)) := 3.14159265 * r * r       # r used twice — fine, it's val
+fn area(Square(s)) := s * s
+
+# `iso`: a unique, owned handle. On Rust this MOVES (`fn consume(s: Shape)`).
+# On the BEAM it is a USE-ONCE linear value: using it twice along a path is a
+# compile error. This catches "used after consumed" with no borrow checker.
+fn consume(s iso Shape) f64 := area(s)         # ok: `s` consumed exactly once
+
+# The linearity check would REJECT this (iso `s` used twice):
+#   fn bad(s iso Shape) f64 := area(s) + area(s)   # error: {"s", 2}
+
+# `ref`: mutable borrow. On Rust this is `&mut T`. On the BEAM target `ref` is
+# REJECTED in the PoC (no process-local aliasing proof) — emitting a
+# `ref`-parameter function to the BEAM raises at compile time. It is a
+# Rust-superset feature, honestly fenced off rather than faked.
+fn scale(s ref Vec(f64), k f64) Vec(f64) := mul_each(s, k)   # &mut Vec<f64> on Rust
+
+# `tag`: identity only (a pid/ref on the BEAM, a borrow on Rust). Shareable;
+# you can observe identity but the value's contents are not owned.
+fn same(a tag Shape, b tag Shape) bool := a == b
+
+# Field capabilities work too: a struct field marked `iso` makes the whole
+# type non-`Clone` on Rust (only `Debug`), because the field is unique.
+struct Buffer(data iso Vec(u8), len val i64)
+
+# NOTE on the BEAM linearity model (PoC scope): the checker is TOTAL over every
+# node the parser produces and is BRANCH-AWARE for `if` — a value consumed once
+# in each arm counts as consumed once (`max` over arms), so a move-per-branch is
+# legal, while a double-use within a single arm is still rejected. The same
+# `max` rule extends to `match`-expression bodies once they lower through this
+# checker (today `match` is handled at the clause level, not as a counted node).
+# See docs/spec/capability-lowering.md.

+# ===========================================================================
+# 05 — Modules, visibility & imports
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: a Rian module is an ORDINARY BEAM module — MFA interop is free in
+# both directions with no shim (`rian_geometry:area(..)` from Erlang,
+# `:rian_geometry.area(..)` from Elixir). Items are private by default; `pub`
+# exports them.
+#
+# `.` is the single, universal qualifier (ADR-0029): module calls, variant
+# paths, and field access all use `.`, disambiguated by the CASE of operands —
+# exactly Elixir's own rule. (`::` is still accepted as a transitional alias.)
+#
+# Spec: docs/spec/modules.md · ADR: docs/adr/0029-dot-syntax.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+mod Geometry do
+  use Math                     # qualified import  -> Math.pi
+  use Std.(Vec, sqrt)          # unqualified import of selected names
+
+  # `pub const` is exported with an accessor on the BEAM and `pub const` on Rust.
+  pub const TAU f64 := 6.28318530
+
+  # `pub type` exports the type and its constructors.
+  pub type Shape := Circle(radius f64) | Square(side f64)
+
+  # Public, multi-clause. `Math.pi` is a cross-module call (Pascal head, lower
+  # name) — it lowers to `Math.pi` on Elixir and `math::pi()` on Rust.
+  pub fn area(Shape) f64
+  pub fn area(Circle(r)) := Math.pi * r * r
+  pub fn area(Square(s)) := s * s
+
+  pub fn perimeter(Shape) f64
+  pub fn perimeter(Circle(r)) := TAU * r
+  pub fn perimeter(Square(s)) := 4.0 * s
+
+  # Private helper (no `pub`): becomes `defp` on Elixir, a non-`pub fn` on Rust.
+  fn square(x f64) f64 := x * x
+end
+
+# Disambiguation summary (resolved at emit time, by operand case):
+#
+#   Geometry.area(x)   Rian module fn   -> Elixir Geometry.area(x) | Rust geometry::area(x)
+#   Value.Num(n)       type/variant     -> Elixir {:num, n}        | Rust Value::Num(n)
+#   point.x            field access     -> Elixir point.x          | Rust point.x
+#   :lists.sum(xs)     Erlang FFI       -> Elixir :lists.sum(xs)   | (BEAM-only)
+#   String.upcase(s)   Elixir-lib FFI   -> Elixir String.upcase(s) | (BEAM-only)

+# ===========================================================================
+# 06 — Macros & comptime: metaprogramming without quote/unquote
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: macros are DECLARATIVE pattern->template (the `macro_rules!` /
+# `syntax-rules` model), NOT Elixir-style `quote`/`unquote` AST construction.
+# Both macros and `comptime` are pure AST->AST passes that run BEFORE typecheck,
+# so they need no parser changes and work uniformly for the BEAM and Rust.
+#
+# ADR: docs/adr/0030-macros.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# A declarative macro: parameters are substituted as AST (never as text). The
+# template is ordinary Rian code.
+macro unless(cond, body) => if not cond do body else 0 end
+macro square(x)          => x * x
+
+# Two guarantees fall out of substituting at the AST level:
+#
+# 1. NO PRECEDENCE BUGS. `square(a + b)` expands to `(a + b) * (a + b)`, never
+#    the C-preprocessor disaster `a + b * a + b`. The precedence-aware emitter
+#    parenthesizes automatically.
+#
+# 2. HYGIENE BY DEFAULT. A template's own binders are gensym-renamed, so they
+#    cannot capture the caller's variables. In the macro below, the template's
+#    `tmp` becomes `tmp__h<N>` and will NOT clobber a caller's `tmp`.
+macro add_tmp(x) => if true do tmp := 100; x + tmp else 0 end
+
+# Usage looks like an ordinary call:
+fn demo_unless(n i64) i64 := unless(n > 5, n * 10)   # n=3 -> 30 ; n=7 -> 0
+fn demo_square(a i64, b i64) i64 := square(a + b)    # (a+b)*(a+b)
+fn demo_hygiene(tmp i64) i64 := add_tmp(tmp)         # 5 -> 105 (NOT 200)
+
+# `comptime(expr)`: evaluate a constant expression at compile time and replace
+# it with its literal (the Zig model). The evaluator is a PURE SANDBOX:
+# literals, arithmetic, boolean and comparison operators only.
+fn table_size() i64 := comptime(2 + 3 * 4)           # becomes the literal 14
+fn scaled() i64     := comptime((1 + 2) * 5)          # becomes 15
+fn always() bool    := comptime(3 > 5)                # becomes false
+
+# The sandbox REFUSES effects at compile time (each of these is a compile error):
+#   comptime(foo(3))            # calls are not allowed in a pure comptime sandbox
+#   comptime(x + 1)             # `x` is not a compile-time constant
+#   comptime(:lists.sum(xs))    # FFI is not pure — refused
+#
+# There is no build-time effect without an explicit (and currently deferred)
+# build capability. Purity is the default and the guarantee.

+# ===========================================================================
+# 07 — FFI: interop is free on the BEAM
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: a Rian module compiles to a BEAM module, so calling any
+# Erlang/Elixir function is just emitting `Module:function(..)` — no shim, no
+# binding layer. Rian therefore ships NO stdlib yet; it leans on the target
+# libraries and adds exactly one primitive: the FFI call. FFI is BEAM-only
+# (no Rust lowering) and is flagged by the subset linter.
+#
+# ADR: docs/adr/0027-fast-track-self-hosting.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Erlang-module FFI: an ATOM head (`:lists`, `:maps`) -> `:lists.fn(..)`.
+# This is exactly Elixir's own convention for calling Erlang.
+fn total(xs val Vec(i64)) i64     := :lists.sum(xs)
+fn rev(xs val Vec(i64)) Vec(i64)  := :lists.reverse(xs)
+
+# Elixir-module FFI: a PascalCase head (`String`, `Enum`, `Integer`) ->
+# `String.fn(..)`. Calls nest naturally.
+fn shout(s val str) str := String.upcase(s)
+fn clean(s val str) str := String.trim(String.downcase(s))
+
+# Higher-order FFI with a Rian lambda passed to an Erlang/Elixir function:
+fn doubled(xs val Vec(i64)) Vec(i64) := Enum.map(xs, (x) -> x * 2)
+fn sum_fold(xs val Vec(i64)) i64     := :lists.foldl((x, acc) -> x + acc, 0, xs)
+
+# Bare FFI calls are typed `dynamic`. An optional `extern` declaration gives a
+# precise type to a hot binding (these typed wrappers are the seed of the
+# eventual Rian stdlib). NOTE: `extern` surface syntax is still an open item —
+# shown here illustratively.
+extern :lists.sum(Vec(i64)) i64
+extern String.upcase(str) str
+
+# Because the emitted module is an ordinary BEAM module, the reverse direction
+# is free too: Erlang calls `rian_text:shout("hi")` and Elixir calls
+# `:rian_text.shout("hi")` with no wrapper.

+# ===========================================================================
+# 08 — Lambdas, blocks & collection literals
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: the three features that complete the self-hosting subset —
+# lambdas, `if`/block bodies, and list/map literal construction. Each lowers to
+# an idiomatic form per target, and the Rust backend honestly REFUSES the
+# BEAM-only shapes rather than emitting non-idiomatic code.
+#
+# Spec: docs/spec/selfhost-features.md
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Lambdas: `(x) -> e`, `(x, y) -> e`. Disambiguated from grouping by scanning
+# for `->` after the matching `)`.
+#   (x) -> x * 2        Elixir: fn x -> x * 2 end      Rust: |x| x * 2
+#   (x, acc) -> x + acc Elixir: fn x, acc -> ...        Rust: |x, acc| x + acc
+fn map_double(xs val Vec(i64)) Vec(i64) := Enum.map(xs, (x) -> x * 2)
+fn fold_sum(xs val Vec(i64)) i64        := :lists.foldl((x, acc) -> x + acc, 0, xs)
+
+# `if`/block bodies as expressions. Blocks are `;`-separated bindings ending in
+# a value expression.
+fn sign(n i64) i64 := if n >= 0 do 1 else -1 end
+fn step(n i64) i64 := if n > 0 do a := n * 2; a + 1 else 0 end
+
+# List literals lower to `[..]` on Elixir and `vec![..]` on Rust.
+fn small_primes() Vec(i64) := [2, 3, 5, 7]
+
+# Cons CONSTRUCTION `[h | t]` lowers on Elixir (O(1) prepend), but is BEAM-ONLY
+# on Rust (there is no idiomatic `Vec` cons) — the Rust backend refuses it.
+fn prepend(p i64, rest val Vec(i64)) Vec(i64) := [p | rest]
+
+# Map literals are BEAM-only in the PoC (Rust lowering via HashMap/BTreeMap is
+# a future item). Used here on a default (Elixir-target) function.
+fn origin_record() Map := %{x: 0, y: 0}
+
+# These three features plus FFI make the existing front-end
+# (parse -> typecheck-shape -> exhaustiveness -> emit) expressible in Rian
+# itself — the language is now self-hostable in principle; what remains is
+# engineering (the lexer + declaration parser), not language design.

+# ===========================================================================
+# 09 — Capstone: a tiny arithmetic evaluator
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: one small program that exercises Rian's whole personality —
+# a sealed recursive sum type, exhaustive `match`, multi-clause functions with
+# guards, reference capabilities, modules with `pub`, and the
+# portable-core vs BEAM-only boundary. The `eval` core lowers to BOTH targets;
+# the `show` pretty-printer uses FFI and is therefore BEAM-only.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+mod Calc do
+  use Math
+
+  # A sealed, RECURSIVE expression tree. On Rust the recursive fields are
+  # auto-boxed (`Box<Expr>`); on the BEAM these are tagged tuples. Because the
+  # sum is sealed, the exhaustiveness gate can prove `eval` is total.
+  pub type Expr :=
+      Lit(i64)
+    | Add(Expr, Expr)
+    | Mul(Expr, Expr)
+    | Neg(Expr)
+
+  # `iso` Expr: the evaluator consumes the tree it is given (owned `Expr` on
+  # Rust, a use-once handle on the BEAM). Each recursive sub-tree is itself
+  # consumed exactly once along every path — the linearity model is satisfied.
+  pub fn eval(e iso Expr) i64
+  pub fn eval(Lit(n))    := n
+  pub fn eval(Add(a, b)) := eval(a) + eval(b)
+  pub fn eval(Mul(a, b)) := eval(a) * eval(b)
+  pub fn eval(Neg(x))    := -eval(x)
+  # Drop any one clause above and the exhaustiveness gate REFUSES to emit:
+  # a non-total match is a compile error on both targets.
+
+  # `depth` reads the tree without consuming it -> `val` (borrow on Rust,
+  # freely shareable on the BEAM, so `a`/`b` may each be used more than once).
+  pub fn depth(e val Expr) i64
+  pub fn depth(Lit(_))    := 1
+  pub fn depth(Neg(x))    := 1 + depth(x)
+  pub fn depth(Add(a, b)) := 1 + max2(depth(a), depth(b))
+  pub fn depth(Mul(a, b)) := 1 + max2(depth(a), depth(b))
+
+  # Guarded clause backed by an unguarded fallback -> total on both targets.
+  fn max2(i64, i64) i64
+  fn max2(a, b) when a >= b := a
+  fn max2(a, b)             := b
+

+  # `<>` concatenation, so it is part of the BEAM ring, not the portable core.
+  # The subset linter would flag it if this module were marked `@target :rust`.
+  pub fn show(e val Expr) str
+  pub fn show(Lit(n))    := Integer.to_string(n)
+  pub fn show(Neg(x))    := "-(" <> show(x) <> ")"
+  pub fn show(Add(a, b)) := "(" <> show(a) <> " + " <> show(b) <> ")"
+  pub fn show(Mul(a, b)) := "(" <> show(a) <> " * " <> show(b) <> ")"
+end
+
+# A worked term:  (2 + 3) * -4   ==>  eval = -20,  depth = 3
+#   Mul(Add(Lit(2), Lit(3)), Neg(Lit(4)))
+#
+# eval  lowers to idiomatic Elixir AND idiomatic, ownership-checked Rust.
+# show  lowers to Elixir only (FFI is BEAM-only) — the three-ring boundary in
+#       action: one source, two targets, with the non-portable part fenced off
+#       explicitly rather than silently mistranslated.

+# ===========================================================================
+# 10 — Function forms: every way to write a function body
+# ===========================================================================
+# Character: a `fn` body is one of two things, and the choice is purely about
+# size — there is no semantic difference, both yield a value (implicit return):
+#
+#   1.  := expr                      single-expression body  (the one-liner)
+#   2.  <newline> stmts.. expr end   BLOCK body               (multiline)
+#
+# Lambdas `(x) -> e` are the third, anonymous form. Both single-clause and
+# multi-clause functions may use EITHER body form, and a multi-clause group
+# may MIX them clause by clause.
+#
+# Spec: docs/spec/clauses-guards.md §1-2 · docs/spec/expressions.md §1
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# --- (1) single-expression body: `:= expr` --------------------------------
+# Best when the whole function is one expression. This is the form `show`
+# uses in the capstone.
+fn double(n i64) i64 := n * 2
+
+# --- (2) block body: multiline, implicit return ---------------------------
+# Opens after the return type, closes with `end`. Statements are `:=`
+# bindings (single-assignment); the LAST expression is the returned value.
+# There is no `return` keyword — the final expression is the value.
+fn norm(v val Vec(f64)) f64
+  total := v |> sum            # binding
+  n     := len(v)             # binding
+  total / n                   # final expression = the function's value
+end
+
+# A block body can contain `if`/`match` expressions, more bindings, and
+# (capability permitting) local mutation with `<-`. Here a running total is
+# threaded through bindings — shadowing, the immutable default.
+fn stats(xs val Vec(i64)) i64
+  s := :lists.sum(xs)
+  n := len(xs)
+  if n == 0 do 0 else s div n end   # the `if` expression is the value
+end
+
+# --- multi-clause group MIXING both body forms ----------------------------
+# A bodiless signature line, then contiguous pattern clauses. Some clauses are
+# one-liners; the recursive arm uses a block body to introduce a local binding.
+type Tree(T) := Leaf | Node(left Tree(T), value T, right Tree(T))
+
+fn depth(Tree(T)) i64
+fn depth(Leaf) := 0                 # (1) one-liner clause
+fn depth(Node(l, _, r))             # (2) block-body clause
+  dl := depth(l)
+  dr := depth(r)
+  1 + max2(dl, dr)
+end
+
+fn max2(i64, i64) i64
+fn max2(a, b) when a >= b := a
+fn max2(a, b)             := b
+
+# --- (3) lambdas / closures: `(x) -> e` -----------------------------------
+# Anonymous, single-expression. Passed to higher-order functions (usually via
+# FFI). For multi-step logic inside a lambda, the body can be a block
+# EXPRESSION (`if .. do a := ..; .. end`), or factor it into a named `fn`.
+fn map_double(xs val Vec(i64)) Vec(i64) := Enum.map(xs, (x) -> x * 2)
+fn clamp_each(xs val Vec(i64)) Vec(i64) :=
+  Enum.map(xs, (x) -> if x < 0 do 0 else x end)   # block-expression lambda body
+
+# --- the same `show`, written with block-body clauses ---------------------
+# Purely a style choice vs. the capstone's one-liners — identical meaning.
+fn show2(e val Expr) str
+fn show2(Lit(n)) := Integer.to_string(n)
+fn show2(Add(a, b))                  # block body: name the parts, then join
+  ls := show2(a)
+  rs := show2(b)
+  "(" <> ls <> " + " <> rs <> ")"
+end

+# Rian by example
+
+A guided tour of **Rian's surface syntax and character** — a typed,
+capability-disciplined language that lowers the *same source* to two targets:
+idiomatic **Elixir/BEAM** and idiomatic, ownership-checked **Rust**.
+
+> **Status — read this first.** These `.rian` files are **illustrative source**,
+> validated against the specs and ADRs catalogued in the
+> [design corpus](../../docs/README.md) — they are **not yet compilable**. Rian
+> has no lexer or declaration parser yet
+> ([ADR-0031](../../docs/adr/0031-bootstrap-strategy.md), Stage 0.1 — the gate
+> to compiling real files). The compiler's passes today are driven by
+> hand-built IR, demonstrated by the runnable Elixir drivers catalogued in the
+> [project README](../../README.md). This is exactly how the corpus itself
+> presents Rian source: as the surface the verified passes will consume once the
+> parser lands.
+
+## The files
+
+| File | Shows |
+| --- | --- |
+| [01_basics.rian](01_basics.rian) | Expression-orientation, `:=` single-assignment, `if`/blocks, the operator table (`/` vs `div`, `<>`, `\|>`, non-associative comparisons) |
+| [02_types_match.rian](02_types_match.rian) | `type` / `struct` / `alias`, the `match` expression, recursive sums, guarded arms |
+| [03_clauses_guards.rian](03_clauses_guards.rian) | Multi-clause functions, the restricted guard sublanguage, static exhaustiveness, union narrowing, `@partial` |
+| [04_capabilities.rian](04_capabilities.rian) | **The heart of the language** — `val`/`iso`/`ref`/`tag` driving Rust ownership and BEAM linearity, with no lifetimes |
+| [05_modules.rian](05_modules.rian) | `mod`, `pub`, `use`, `const`, and `.` as the universal qualifier |
+| [06_macros_comptime.rian](06_macros_comptime.rian) | Declarative pattern→template macros (hygienic, no `quote`/`unquote`) and the pure `comptime` sandbox |
+| [07_ffi.rian](07_ffi.rian) | Free BEAM interop — atom-head Erlang calls, PascalCase Elixir calls, `extern` typed bindings |
+| [08_lambdas_collections.rian](08_lambdas_collections.rian) | Lambdas, `if`/block bodies, list/map literals, and the BEAM-only refusals on Rust |
+| [09_capstone_calc.rian](09_capstone_calc.rian) | A complete tiny evaluator tying it all together, including the portable-core vs BEAM-only boundary |
+| [10_function_forms.rian](10_function_forms.rian) | Every function body form — `:=` one-liner, multiline **block body** (`… end`), multi-clause groups mixing both, and lambdas |
+
+Suggested reading order is numeric; 04 is the one to linger on — it is what
+distinguishes Rian from "Elixir with different keywords."
+
+### Function body forms
+
+A `fn` body is one of two shapes (no semantic difference — both yield a value
+via implicit return), plus the anonymous lambda form:
+
+```elixir
+fn double(n i64) i64 := n * 2          # 1. single-expression body (the one-liner)
+
+fn norm(v val Vec(f64)) f64            # 2. block body — multiline, last expr is the value
+  total := v |> sum
+  total / len(v)
+end
+
+(x) -> x * 2                           # 3. lambda — anonymous, single-expression
+```
+
+Both single-clause and multi-clause functions may use **either** body form, and
+a multi-clause group may mix them clause by clause (see
+[10_function_forms.rian](10_function_forms.rian)). There is no `return` keyword.
+
+## Syntax cheat-sheet
+
+```elixir
+# comments start with `#`
+
+fn add(x i64, y i64) i64 := x + y          # single clause: typed head is the boundary
+
+fn classify(i64) str                       # bodiless SIGNATURE line ...
+fn classify(0)            := "zero"         # ... followed by contiguous
+fn classify(n) when n > 0 := "positive"    #     pattern-head clauses
+fn classify(_)            := "negative"
+
+name := expr                               # single-assignment binding (shadow, never mutate)
+total <- expr                              # mutation — capability-gated, BEAM-illegal unless local
+
+if c do a else b end                       # `if` is an expression; `else` is REQUIRED in value position
+match x do P -> e   ...   end              # `match` is an expression; arms use `->`, must be exhaustive
+
+(x) -> x * 2                               # lambda
+[1, 2, 3]      [h | t]      %{a: 1}        # list / cons / map literals
+
+type T := A | B(payload f64)               # sealed sum (ADT)
+struct P(x f64, y f64)                     # product / record
+alias Id := i64                            # transparent synonym
+
+fn f(s val Shape) ...   # val (default, borrow) | iso (owned/use-once) | ref (&mut) | tag (identity)
+
+Geometry.area(x)   # Rian module call      point.x         # field access
+Value.Num(n)       # variant path          :lists.sum(xs)  # Erlang FFI (atom head)
+String.upcase(s)   # Elixir-lib FFI
+
+macro square(x) => x * x                   # declarative macro (AST substitution, hygienic)
+comptime(2 + 3 * 4)                        # pure compile-time constant folding -> 14
+```
+
+## Operator precedence (tightest → loosest)
+
+`f(…)` · `.field` › unary `-`/`not` › `* / rem div` › `+ -` › `<>` › `in` ›
+`|>` › `< <= > >=` *(non-assoc)* › `== !=` *(non-assoc)* › `and` › `or` › `<-`.
+
+See [docs/spec/expressions.md](../../docs/spec/expressions.md) for the full table
+and worked consequences.
+
+## Seeing them actually run (today)
+
+Until the parser lands, the verified passes are exercised through Elixir
+drivers that feed hand-built IR equivalent to the source above:
+
+```sh
+mix run examples/lower_run.exs      # area/1: Rian source -> Elixir + Rust, executed
+mix run examples/dot_run.exs        # `.` qualifier lowering + a Value match
+mix run examples/features_run.exs   # lambdas, if/blocks, list/map literals on the BEAM
+mix run examples/macro_run.exs      # macros + comptime, hygiene proven (hyg(5) = 105)
+mix run examples/selfhost_run.exs   # FFI to :lists / String, executed on the BEAM
+mix run examples/cap_run.exs        # capability -> Rust signature matrix + BEAM linearity
+```
+
+Each driver prints the emitted Elixir and Rust for the corresponding `.rian`
+constructs and runs the BEAM output to prove it. The `.rian` files here are the
+human-facing surface those drivers stand in for.
